title: Launchpad: Hybrid GPU scaling Terraform module (ASG + Karpenter) for Private VPC
text:
Launchpad: Hybrid GPU scaling Terraform module (ASG + Karpenter) for Private VPC

description:
Create a reusable Terraform module (internal name: launchpad-gpu-hybrid) that provisions GPU node groups inside Private VPCs and implements a hybrid autoscaling strategy: primary ASG-backed reserved pools for latency-sensitive workloads and Karpenter-managed spot/burst capacity for cost efficiency. The module should support driver/AMI upgrade orchestration, node-level health checks, graceful evictions, and automated failover from Karpenter to ASG when spot capacity is insufficient. It must integrate with Redwood Private networking, IAM roles, and Console observability hooks.

acceptance_criteria:
Module exposes inputs for vpc_id, private_subnet_ids, allowed_gpu_types, reserved_capacity_config, karpenter_profile_config, node_image_id, gpu_driver_daemonset_enabled, and node_labels/taints
Deploys an ASG with launch template compatible with Private images and attaches correct IAM role and node boot scripts
Creates Karpenter Provisioner CRDs via module outputs + optional bootstrap module that wires cloud-provider settings
Provides documented fallback policy: Karpenter attempts spot first; on insufficient capacity requests automatically flow to reserved ASG via webhook/router config
Implements health checks: node kubelet readiness, GPU plugin (nvidia-device-plugin) health probe, and a node-level heartbeat metric exported to Console
Upgrade plan documented: AMI baking pipeline + driver DaemonSet with node drain window and canary rollout instructions
Integration tests exist in infra-ci that run a canary workload, simulate spot reclamation, and validate failover to ASG within defined SLOs

design_decisions:
Hybrid model chosen to balance cost and latency: reserved ASG for 20-40% baseline, Karpenter for elastic burst/spot capacity
Fallback implemented at request-routing layer (reconcile controller) rather than modifying Karpenter internal heuristics to maintain upgrade safety
Use Launch Templates + SSM parameter for GPU driver bootstrap to keep AMI churn low and allow driver upgrades via DaemonSet when safe
Expose a minimal surface area in Terraform: high-level reserved_capacity and karpenter_profile to avoid frequent breaking changes

implementation_notes:
Terraform module will create: IAM role for nodes, ASG + launch template, security group attachments, autoscaling policies, optional SSM parameter for AMI id, outputs for karpenter provisioning (provisioner manifest + tls bootstrap secret refs)
Karpenter integration will be opt-in via module flag `enable_karpenter_provisioner`. When enabled the module emits a YAML artifact to S3/GCS and returns the artifact URL in outputs for the Private control plane to apply
Health checks: Install a lightweight node-health DaemonSet that reports node status to the Console via metrics endpoint (Prometheus exporter). Terraform will provision RBAC and ServiceAccount for the exporter.
Driver upgrades: default flow is AMI bake (preferred) with optional in-place driver DaemonSet update for urgent patches. Provide documented preflight checks (kernel version match, CUDA compatibility matrix)

risks_and_mitigations:
Spot eviction causing temporary capacity loss -> mitigation: conservative reserved baseline (configurable) + quick failover router to ASG
Karpenter/ASG lifecycle mismatch -> mitigation: node taints and topology labels to ensure pods land on correct pools; controller reconciler handles reassignments
GPU driver mismatches during upgrades -> mitigation: gating tests in infra-ci that validate sample inference jobs on candidate AMIs and driver combinations
Terraform drift on provisioned CRDs -> mitigation: outputs-only approach for Karpenter artifacts with apply handled by Private control plane; also add drift-detection job in infra-ci

testing_plan:
Unit tests: Terraform module linting with tflint and validate against terraform 1.5.x
Integration: deploy into a staging Private VPC (ci/staging) with 2 g4dn nodes and 4 spot-backed g5 nodes. Run inference workload to establish baseline latency/cost.
Chaos: simulate spot reclamation and node termination to verify failover to ASG within 90s and no pod failures for high-priority classes
Upgrade test: bake new AMI, run canary on 10% of reserved nodes, verify driver compatibility, then promote
Observability: ensure Console dashboard shows tokenized cost breakdown and node-level latency metrics during tests

rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (dev): Module merged behind feature flag, deployed to dev-private clusters; manual verification
Phase 1 (staging): Run full integration + chaos testing, validate metrics and alerts
Phase 2 (pilot): Enable for 1 customer/test team with 50% baseline reserved capacity; monitor for 2 weeks
Phase 3 (wide): Default module recommended in Private onboarding templates; telemetry collection enabled for 30 days before GA

observability_and_slos:
Define SLOs: pod scheduling latency 99th <= 2s for reserved workloads, failover time from Karpenter shortage to ASG <= 90s
Dashboards: Node pool capacity, kernel/driver mismatch alerts, GPU utilization heatmaps, spot eviction rate, node-reboot frequency
Alerts: high node failure rate (>3 nodes in 10min), driver-compatibility errors marked critical

rollback_plan:
If driver upgrade causes regressions: revert DaemonSet and trigger ASG rolling replacement to previous AMI
If hybrid policy causes instability: flip module flag to `reserved_only=true` and scale up ASG baseline; disable Karpenter provisioner artifact application
Automated rollback steps documented in Confluence with runbook links

comments:
2026-02-13 - Aisha Patel: Scoped initial module API and added inputs for `reserved_capacity_pct` and `karpenter_burst_profile`. Need PM sign-off on cost trade-offs before estimate is finalized.
2026-02-18 - Marco Diaz: Prototype Terraform resources for ASG + launch template submitted in PR #1823. Early tests show successful node join but driver bootstrap failed on kernel mismatch in one AMI variant.
2026-02-25 - Lenore Wu (Infra Eng): Reviewed PR, requested adding SSM parameterization for AMI id and stronger IAM least-privilege for node role. Also requested outputs for next-step automation.
2026-03-02 - Security: Flagged need for KMS encryption for SSM parameters and audit logging for node lifecycle events. Marked security_review_required=true.
2026-03-09 - Marco Diaz: Added canary flow and integration tests. Chaos test job passes in staging for baseline config (reserved 30%, karpenter enabled). Noted two follow-ups: improve exporter resiliency and throttle Karpenter provisioning rate to avoid API quota spikes.
2026-03-12 - Product (Ravi Kumar): Approved pilot for internal teams. Requested default reserved baseline be set to 25% for new customers.
